newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae sees little change in 1997 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae sees little change in 1997 EPS.

text.p: Fannie Mae said Thursday it expects very little change in its earnings per share growth for 1997 as long as interest rates remain steady.

"Our expectations for the year is that within a reasonable range we will have very little change in our net interest income or EPS growth for 1997," said Tim Howard, executive vice president and chief financial officer for Fannie Mae.
Howard told reporters after an investor conference the expectations were based on interest rates remaining in a reasonable range of plus or minus 150 basis points.

Last month Fannie Mae reported earnings for the first quarter of 1997 at $734.1 million or $0.67 per common share. This compares with earnings of $654.2 million or $0.59 per common share for the first quarter of 1996.
Howard said he does not expect Fannie Mae to have any difficulty "continuing to add to our strength in double-digit growth in earnings per share" in 1998.
Fannie Mae did not issue a forecast for the second quarter of 1997.
